decisions.choice: Kiriath-arba: the old name of Hebron
decisions.reason: Kiriath-arba is Hebron (Genesis 23:2; Joshua 14:15), the chief town of the hill country of Judah. The list uses the old names of several towns.

decisions.choice: the villages with their fields: the start of a list of towns outside Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Verses 25-30 name the places where people of Judah lived, and verses 31-35 those of Benjamin. Many of Judah's towns lie in the far south of Judah's old land (Joshua 15:21-36), beyond what the province of Judah seems to have held at this time, so the list may show where families had their old homes and land.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the smaller settlements around a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the villages that depended on it, as children on a mother (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45). They are distinct from the open "villages" (verses 25, 30), which had no walls.

decisions.choice: its surrounding towns (Balanced); the towns around it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "its daughters"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: "sus hijas" (L); "sus poblaciones vecinas" (B); "los pueblos de alrededor" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of a town's "daughters"; Balanced and Readable say what they are (meaning decision m3), and keep "aldeas" for the open villages.

decisions.choice: « ses filles » (L); « les localités qui en dépendaient » (B); « les villes autour » (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture; Balanced says that the smaller places depended on the town (meaning decision m3); « villages » stays for the open villages.

decisions.choice: "binti zake" (L); "vitongoji vyake" (B); "miji inayouzunguka" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture; Balanced uses the word for the settlements belonging to a town, and "vijiji" stays for the open villages.

decisions.choice: "các con gái của nó" (L); "các thị trấn chung quanh" (B); "các thị trấn quanh đó" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture, which meaning decision m3 explains; "làng" stays for the open villages.

decisions.choice: "그 딸들" (L); "그 주변 성읍들" (B); "그 둘레의 성읍들" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture; Balanced and Readable say what the "daughters" are, and "마을" stays for the open villages. Balanced and Readable hold the verb for the end of the list (verse 30).

decisions.choice: as suas filhas (L); os seus povoados (B); os povoados ao redor (R); as aldeias
decisions.reason: For verses 25-31: a town's "daughters" are the smaller places that depended on it (m3), as Joshua 15:45 has them in Portuguese, Literal keeping the picture and Balanced and Readable saying "povoados"; "cidades" would confuse them with the towns of the list. The open settlements are "aldeias", as there.

decisions.choice: "ሴቶች ልጆቿ" (Literal) for a town's "daughters", as 2 Chronicles 13:19 on main; "በዙሪያዋ ያሉት ከተሞች" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Literal keeps the Hebrew figure; the other levels say what it means, as the English does. The same holds for verses 27-31.

decisions.choice: Literal and Balanced say "የተቀመጡት / የኖሩት በ..." ("those who lived ... lived in ...") so that the list of towns can run through verse 30 and close there
alternatives: The verb at the end of each verse
decisions.reason: Amharic puts the verb last; the Hebrew list runs over six verses, and each verse must keep its own towns. The Benjamin list (31-35) does the same.

decisions.reason: A town's daughters are the smaller settlements around it (meaning m3); Literal keeps the Hebrew picture, as 1 Chronicles 2:23 and 18:1 do in this translation, and Balanced and Readable say what it means. The same through verse 31.

decisions.choice: "её дочери" (L); "окрестные города" (B); "города вокруг" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of a town's daughters; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does, through 11:25-31.

decisions.reason: The English B and R say surrounding towns here (2 Chronicles has 村々 where its English says villages).

decisions.reason: As the English.

decisions.choice: Lachish, Azekah: fortified towns of the foothills
decisions.reason: Lachish and Azekah were among the last cities of Judah to hold out against Babylon (Jeremiah 34:7). Zanoah and Adullam are in the same region (Joshua 15:34-35).

decisions.choice: encamped: settled, perhaps in a temporary way
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to pitch camp. Here it means that they made their homes over this whole area; it may suggest that the settlements were still small and not fully rebuilt.

decisions.choice: from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom: from the far south to the edge of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The valley of Hinnom runs along the south side of Jerusalem and marked the border between Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:8). Judah's settlements reached from there to Beersheba.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the smaller settlements around a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the villages that depended on it, as children on a mother (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45). They are distinct from the open "villages" (verses 25, 30), which had no walls.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah; in the south; by Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names who settled and where the two places are, so the reader sees the span of the land.

decisions.choice: from Geba: from Geba onward, the starting point of Benjamin's towns
alternatives: those from Geba lived in Micmash ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short: "the sons of Benjamin from Geba". It most likely means that Benjamin's people lived from Geba on, in the towns that follow. Geba was the northern limit of Judah in the time of the kings (2 Kings 23:8).

decisions.choice: Aija, Bethel: Ai and Bethel north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Aija is a form of Ai, near Bethel (Joshua 7:2). Men of Bethel and Ai were among the returned exiles (7:32). Micmash too is near (1 Samuel 13:2).

decisions.choice: its daughters: the smaller settlements around a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the villages that depended on it, as children on a mother (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45). They are distinct from the open "villages" (verses 25, 30), which had no walls.

decisions.choice: lived from Geba onward
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb from verse 25 and say how "from Geba" relates to the names that follow. Literal keeps the bare Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "Aía"
decisions.reason: Aija is a form of Ai (meaning decision m2); the text's own form is kept, as in the English.

decisions.choice: Aia
decisions.reason: The Hebrew spells the name of Ai with a longer form here (m2); Portuguese writes "Aia", keeping "Ai" for the usual form (Ezra 2:28; Nehemiah 7:32).

decisions.choice: "ዓያ" for Aija; "ማክማስ" (Micmash) as Ezra 2:27
decisions.reason: The meaning decision takes Aija to be Ai, but the Hebrew spells it differently, so the Amharic keeps the spelling apart, as the English does.

decisions.choice: divisions of Judah to Benjamin: some Levite groups of Judah settled in Benjamin
alternatives: some divisions of the Levites belonged to Judah and some to Benjamin
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very brief. It most likely says that some divisions of Levites, counted with Judah, were settled among Benjamin. It could also mean that the Levites were shared between the two tribes' towns. The Levites had no land of their own and lived in towns among the other tribes (Numbers 35:2-8).

decisions.choice: turmas (L, B); grupos (R)
decisions.reason: "As turmas" is the word Chronicles uses in Portuguese for the divisions of priests and Levites (1 Chronicles 24); Readable says "grupos", as the English Readable says "groups".

decisions.choice: machleqot "組" (every level)
decisions.reason: As 1 Chronicles.
